title: Apply for a producer/wholesaler liquor licence
summary: This page provides information on how to apply for a producer/wholesaler liquor licence if you are a liquor producer or wholesaler.
intro:
You need to apply for the producer/wholesaler liquor licence if you're a liquor producer, such as a winemaker, brewer or distiller, or a liquor wholesaler, and you want to sell alcohol to other liquor licensees.

The licence also allows producers to:

Wholesalers are not able to sell to the general public.

For up-to-date liquor licence guidelines, resources and tools visit Liquor & Gaming NSW liquor licensing.

If you have questions or feedback about liquor licensing contact Liquor & Gaming NSW.
who_can_apply: Must not be suspended or disqualified from holding a liquor licence.
what_you_need: A OneGov account or MyServiceNSW Account.
A floor plan showing the proposed boundaries for the licensed area.
Details of the proposed licensee, premises, and business owner.
Contact details for you or another authorised person.
A copy of your development approval or consent (if applicable).
Evidence of Responsible Service of Alcohol (RSA) qualifications.
A current National Police Check certificate issued within the last 3 months.
The 3 identity documents used when applying for the National Police Check.
The names and birthdates of all directors and officeholders (if it is a proprietary company).
A current Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) extract.
Details of an appointment of manager notice.
If applying as an individual, additional required documents apply.
If applying as an organisation, additional required documents apply.

how_to_steps.text: Ensure you have gathered the required documents.
Log in or create an account.
Follow the prompts to complete and submit your application.

more_info.text: Once your application is lodged, you will be sent a public site notice. You need to attach the notice to your premises until the application is granted. Council, police and agency stakeholders will be automatically notified of your application. You must notify neighbouring premises within a 50-metre radius of your venue.
If you wish to complete the site notice manually at your convenience before you lodge your application, you can download a the site notice form.
Under certain circumstances, more than one premises can be allowed under the one licence. You will need to apply for and gain your licence before you can apply for additional premises.

Licences can be tailored to your needs by apply for authorisations and exemptions. For example, you can apply for extended trading hours or an on-premises drinking authorisation. See more detail on the Liquor & Gaming NSW website.

Conditions apply to NSW liquor licences. Some are statutory conditions that apply automatically depending on the type of premises. Other conditions may be imposed on a licence by the Independent Liquor & Gaming Authority. You can apply for alternate or additional conditions using the Licence conditions form: producer/wholesaler – PDF. Lodging this form with your application may reduce processing time.

faqs.q: Who can apply for a producer/wholesaler liquor licence?
faqs.a: Applicants must be 18 years or older, and not suspended or disqualified from holding a liquor licence.

faqs.q: What is the purpose of this licence?
faqs.a: This licence allows liquor producers (like winemakers, brewers, or distillers) or liquor wholesalers to sell alcohol to other liquor licensees. Wholesalers cannot sell to the general public.

faqs.q: Where can I find up-to-date guidelines for liquor licences?
faqs.a: For up-to-date liquor licence guidelines, resources, and tools, visit the Liquor & Gaming NSW liquor licensing page.
